paper_title: Getting More Out of Black Hole Superradiance: a Statistically Rigorous Approach to Ultralight Boson Constraints from Black Hole Spin Measurements
notes: 95% credible region (highest posterior density) for the inverse ULB decay constant f^-1 vs boson mass mu from black-hole superradiance of the supermassive BH IRAS 09149-6206 (tau_BH = 450 Myr), the paper's novel constraint ('first ULB constraints derived from IRAS 09149-6206'). Extracted from the vector paths of the left panel of Fig. 4 (e-print figures/exclusions.pdf), solid contour = equilibrium self-interaction scenario (the paper's preferred treatment; the dashed bosenova contour extends about one order of magnitude higher in f^-1). The excluded region lies BELOW/INSIDE this arch-shaped boundary: masses ~8.8e-20 to ~6e-19 eV are excluded for f^-1 below the curve, down to the prior edge f^-1 ~ 1e-19 GeV^-1 (prior restricted to f < M_Pl). Points follow the contour from bottom-left up over the arch to bottom-right, so the near-vertical edges contain several points at almost equal mass. The paper also derives an analogous (stronger) contour for M33 X-7 (right panel of Fig. 4), covering mu ~ 1.7e-13 to 3e-12 eV, which overlaps existing literature bounds; the IRAS 09149-6206 region is the new result reported here. Not a dark-matter-density-dependent limit; no rescaling applied. Axis calibration from exact tick-mark positions in the PDF.
